Author: dajoey
Name: PvP Solver
Description: PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.
Changelog:
v0.1.2.36 (2026-11-25)
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTargetAreaFriend: ground-targeted beneficial placement now snaps to the terrain and is kept inside the action's range and the player's line of sight before it is used (upstream RotationSolverReborn 'Fix for ground targeting actions', ported onto the fork's carried ground-target subsystem). Spots the old code took at face value - saved beneficial positions, the tank's position, the point between the player and the attacked party member - can no longer land behind a wall or under the floor.
- After the server rejects a ground-targeted action, the ground-target finder targets the player's own position for five seconds before trying the placement again. The rejection is read from the existing ActorControl hook (ActionTimeline/ActionTimelineManager.cs, category 0x2BC, second argument 1) and recorded in DataCenter (Basic/DataCenter.cs _actionRejectedTicks), matching upstream's Watcher feed.
- The tank and saved-spot steps of the ground-target finder were restructured into upstream's helper shape (FindTargetAreaTank with a two-pass stance scan and an effect-range check, FindBeneficialPosition with a flat-distance gate, TryGetGroundPosition with a 0.5-range margin); the boss-position step and the arena-center fallback upstream added are NOT ported - the fork removed them as PvE remnants in v0.1.2.30. The 'Use beneficial ground-targeted actions' setting's description (Basic/Configuration/Configs.cs) now describes the fork's actual fallback order.
- UI/RotationConfigWindow.cs: the 'Add position' button places the saved spot through the same terrain-snap helper (ObjectHelper.SnapToGround) instead of its own inline raycast, and Basic/Helpers/ObjectHelper.cs extracts that raycast into one shared Raycast helper that also serves line-of-sight checks.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.35 (2026-11-22)
- Basic/Helpers/StatusHelper.cs LocksActions: action-locking statuses are now detected reliably - Out of the Action (statuses 1113, 1284 and 1462) counts as locking actions even when the game data sheet does not flag it, and a status with no remaining time counts as still active instead of expiring instantly. Rotation updates now pause correctly through those lockout states (read by Updaters/ActionUpdater.cs).
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTarget and GetCanTargets, and Basic/Actions/BaseAction.cs and IBaseAction.cs CanUse, accept an optional extra target filter passed by the caller; no built-in PvP action passes one yet, so target selection behaves exactly as before. This keeps the engine aligned with upstream RotationSolverReborn for future fixes.
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_BasicInfo.cs adds a ShouldDelayCommandAction hook, checked by the commanded-action paths in CustomRotation_Ability.cs and CustomRotation_GCD.cs before firing a commanded action immediately; the default answer is no, so commanded actions fire exactly as before.

v0.1.2.34 (2026-11-21)
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the chooser never called the job rotations' GeneralGCD, so no attack GCD was ever selected - the character could only auto-heal, Guard, Recuperate and drink the elixir, which read as healing instead of attacking in matches. The call was deleted together with the duty-rotation engine in v0.1.2.23 (the same class of loss as the v0.1.2.32 rotation-load fix), so every version from v0.1.2.23 to v0.1.2.33 shipped with attack GCDs as dead code. GeneralGCD is called again inside the NoCasting branch, in upstream's chooser order (heals first, attacks after).
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the DefenseArea and DefenseSingle branches were emptied by the same removal, so the healer PvP rotations' defense GCD overrides were equally unreachable; both calls are restored. No duty-rotation, Provoke or other PvE machinery returns.
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs DoAction: every executed-action change now leaves one "ActionTap: <name> (<id>)" log line (on-change only, so it cannot spam). This makes the live-path release check possible: a real match must show attack actions being chosen before any build is called good.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/SelectionGate.cs: the release harness now fails when the compiled chooser no longer calls GeneralGCD (IL call-site count and position after the heal branch), when the ability chooser loses GeneralAbility, when any shipped PvP rotation loses its attack-bearing GeneralGCD override, or when the ActionTap log line is missing from the built assembly.

v0.1.2.33 (2026-11-21)
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs UpdateRotationState: "Turn on when a match starts" could never engage - it only ran during the match loading screen, when no player object exists and the job role is unknown, so the null-player early return and the job-role check silently dropped it and the rotation loaded but never acted in matches. The auto-on now latches during the load screen (new pure decision core Basic/Decisions/MatchStartAutoOn.cs) and engages the PvP state on the first cycle where the player and job are loaded, logging both steps.
- RotationSolverPlugin.cs constructor and Commands/RSCommands_BasicInfo.cs RSCommands.Enable: the /pvpsolver, /pvs, "/pvpsolver Auto" and "/pvpsolver Off" handlers were registered only near the end of a 10-30 second start-up (after nine windows, the icon cache and the status lists), so commands typed while the plugin was still starting read as "Command not found". Registration now runs first, right after the configuration loads, and a start-up log line lists every command and its registration result.
- Commands/RSCommands_StateSpecialCommand.cs UpdateState and DoOneCommandType: rotation state changes and ignored role-less commands are logged, so a state that silently never engages can no longer hide behind a clean log.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/MatchStartAutoOnCases.cs and Cases/CommandGate.cs: the release harness now fails the build when a documented slash command has no registration call site in the built assembly (IL call-site count, not just source text), when the constructor no longer registers before the slow init steps, or when the match-start auto-on decision core cannot engage from the loading-screen conditions the shipped bug produced.

v0.1.2.32 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- Fixed: rotations never loaded, so the plugin did nothing in PvP matches since v0.1.2.26. The duty-rotation engine removal (v0.1.2.23) had also removed the single call in Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs LoadBuiltInRotations that fills CustomRotations from the assembly scan (LoadCustomRotationGroup); the rotation list stayed empty, the log stopped right after "MajorUpdater: triggering rotation load..." and no rotation was ever selected, with no error line anywhere.
- Restored that call and the "LoadBuiltInRotations: found N rotation groups" log line; a scan that finds no rotation groups now logs an error instead of staying silent (Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs, LoadBuiltInRotations).
- Added a release-harness gate (tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness, RotationLoaderWiring) that fails when the rotation-load wiring is severed or the shipped assembly contains no loadable rotation - the regression class that passed every existing gate in v0.1.2.26 - v0.1.2.31.
- No PvE rotation content or behaviour returns; the PvP-only scope is unchanged. Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.31 (2026-11-20) [testing]
- Round 6 completion: the post-release marker grep still found four generated StatusID entries whose description text carries a marker word (ThrownForALoop, Soteria, BackFromTheBrink, BannerOfHonedAcuity). All four are unreferenced PvE statuses and are removed from the generated table; no code reads them.
- No code change and no PvP behaviour change; every remaining marker hit is a cited part of a PvP path (the Sage Kardia and Dancer partner targeting, and the tank lock-on VFX check).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
